clue.text: Descend shaft and be enthusiastically received

definitions.meaning: to drop down a shaft dug for water is to make a descent into it
to be warmly welcomed by an audience or meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means climbing into a water shaft, and idiomatically means to win approval or a warm response.

clue.text: In some degree, Celts make a nation

indicators.note: in some of the words says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that Celtic peoples, to some extent, form a nation of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'make a nation' as the definition, but 'make' cannot stand for a country; it is the link (the letters make a nation), and 'In some' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a sovereign country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Arrest foreign character in row

indicators.note: in places the foreign character inside the word for row

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A police officer seizing a foreigner who was caught in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest someone is to hold them in custody.

clue.text: With great bitterness, cleans out prison

parts.note: wormwood is a very bitter plant, and the word means bitter grief
to scrub is to clean thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone resentfully tidying out a jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: WORMWOOD SCRUBS is a well-known men's prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a London jail, an example of a prison.

clue.text: Criminal not the correct perpetrator?

parts.note: something not correct is wrong
the perpetrator of an act is its doer

explanation.surface: A suspicion that police have arrested the wrong culprit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is an offender, someone who breaks the law.

clue.text: Flits around and steals

indicators.note: around tells us to move the letters of flits about

explanation.surface: A thief darting here and there and pocketing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for pilfering it.

clue.text: Violently eject from second seat

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in church

explanation.surface: Someone being thrown out of the second seat with force.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to throw something out in a forceful stream, as when vomiting.

clue.text: Ring up twice, getting ridicule

indicators.note: twice says the reversed piece appears two times in a row
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the word is backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Making two phone calls in order to mock someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like a telephone call; 'up' reverses HOOP to POOH, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to dismiss it scornfully.

clue.text: Combat uniform for guard

parts.note: combat is fighting, war
dress is formal attire, as in battledress

explanation.surface: Camouflage fatigues issued to a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a female prison officer, a jail guard.

clue.text: Even king Alfred's cooking to be so popular?

definitions.text: Even king Alfred's cooking to be so popular?

parts.words: Even king Alfred's cooking to be so popular?
parts.note: legend says King Alfred let a peasant woman's cakes burn while he brooded, so his baking was hot indeed; selling quickly is the idiom

explanation.surface: Wondering whether even King Alfred's notoriously burnt baking could become a bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred the Great, an English king, is said to have burnt cakes left in his care while hiding from the Danes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sell very fast, as fresh-baked goods do.

clue.text: Chemical compound husband got out of good book

indicators.note: got out of says the husband leaves the book's name

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: A man climbing out of a Bible to become a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Red for footballer makes him a bit sick

parts.note: a red card for a footballer means being sent off
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A red card leaves a footballer feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a sending-off; the clue reads 'Red' as a COLOUR and the footballer's fate as OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off colour means slightly unwell.

clue.text: Feature with wit in conversation

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a wag is a joker, a wit

explanation.surface: A witty remark appearing in someone's talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is informal British slang for a chat.

clue.text: Captain who exercises with rope

definitions.meaning: the master of a ship or team leader
one who jumps a skipping rope for fitness

explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is a word for a ship's master, and literally a person skipping.

clue.text: TV programme to find father of the year?

definitions.meaning: a long-running BBC chart music show
pops are fathers, so the best dad would rank first among them

explanation.surface: A talent show looking for the best dad of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP OF THE POPS was the BBC's weekly pop-chart show; 'pops' is informal for dads.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a British music show, and literally the leading father.

clue.text: As the only difference, I must come in for a bit of retaliation

definitions.text: As the only difference, I must come in for a bit of retaliation

parts.words: As the only difference, I must come in for a bit of retaliation
parts.note: two three-letter words differ only in their middle, where I takes the place of A, and the phrase linking them by for means getting even

explanation.surface: A rule that the only change is that I must enter in exchange for a little revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A in TAT for I and you get TIT; the phrase 'I for A' describes the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, paying back like with like.

clue.text: Pays for development of cafes and inn

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of cafes and inn are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: An investor funding the building of a cafe and an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a project is to fund it.

clue.text: Trip and collapse in sandal

parts.note: a flip is a short pleasure trip
to flop is to collapse or fall

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling and falling while wearing beach sandals.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flop is a thong-style rubber sandal.

clue.text: Insult tailor's bad figure

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled into a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a tailor's poor physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure in a book is a diagram or picture.

clue.text: Work on it for a change — it's an alternative

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: for a change tells us to rearrange the letters of on and it

explanation.surface: Advice to try a different approach for variety.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice among possibilities.

clue.text: Head off fight with English PM

indicators.note: head off removes the first letter of the word for fight

parts.note: a battle is a fight

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister averting a clash with England.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951. 'Head off' takes B from BATTLE, leaving ATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a postwar British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Dreams of snakes, full of passion

indicators.note: full of says the snakes hold the passion inside them

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Fevered nightmares about serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire to something is to long for it ambitiously.

clue.text: Crawled before one religious teacher

indicators.note: before puts the swimming word ahead of the one

parts.note: to do the crawl stroke is to swim
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A holy man who crept along ahead of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests creeping, but here it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu spiritual guru.

clue.text: To bovine animal, say, I attribute part of skull

indicators.note: say tells us the word for the bovine animal is taken by sound

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal
to put something down to a cause is to attribute it

explanation.surface: Someone blaming a cow for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the back of the head, the rear of the cranium.

clue.text: Rebel can't turn into leader of rite

indicators.note: turn into says the letters are transformed into another word

explanation.surface: A rebel being unable to become the one who leads a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the priest who officiates at a religious service.

clue.text: Shrimplike creatures still round the river

indicators.note: round puts the word for still around the river

parts.note: to still a living thing can mean to kill it

explanation.surface: Small crustaceans lying motionless near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans eaten by whales.

clue.text: Clan prepared to seize power

indicators.note: to seize says the prepared word grabs and holds the power

parts.note: set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: A tribe getting ready for a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch of a family or clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: A-level set with intelligence and intuition

parts.note: the sixth form is the school year group studying for A-levels
sense means good judgement, intelligence

explanation.surface: Senior pupils who are both clever and perceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, A-levels are taken in the sixth form, the final two years before university.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is a supposed extra faculty of perception, an intuitive knack.
